thread:
megan (People Ops): Heads up — we just received a PERM audit notice for Priya's green card application. DOL gave us 5 business days to respond. Can we coordinate docs and the hire/start logistics?

priya (Newhire): Yikes. How bad is this for my start date? I was hoping to join full-time next Monday.

raj (Hiring Manager): @megan thanks for flagging. We can't delay the project much. Is there a short-term workaround? contractor? temp offer?

alex (Immigration Counsel): Hi all — PERM audits are not uncommon. DOL timeline varies but the 5-day response window is for the employer to submit recruitment and audit materials. It doesn't automatically stop the I-485, but it can indirectly affect downstream steps.

sam (Finance): If we need to convert Priya to contractor payroll temporarily, we need approval and vendor setup. That typically takes 2–3 business days if we have docs.

onboard-bot: Reminder — benefits enrollment deadline is 30 days from start date. If start is pushed, benefits enrollment will need manual adjustment.

megan (People Ops): Action items I need from everyone: (1) Priya — please upload signed offer + resume + any public job postings you used. (2) Raj — we need copies of the job ad screenshots, recruitment logs, and the internal job description. (3) Alex — can you draft the audit response language?

priya (Newhire): Uploading offer and resume now to the secure folder: https://secure.redwood.example/perm/PRIYA. Also attaching my LinkedIn and previous employer verification emails.

raj (Hiring Manager): I grabbed the job posts — Indeed + LinkedIn + our careers page. Dropped screenshots into the same folder. Also attaching interview matrix.

alex (Immigration Counsel): Draft is started. Quick checklist for DOL response (copying here):
```
- Final job description and minimum requirements used in recruitment
- Copies/snapshots of all external job postings (dates posted)
- Internal recruitment log (names interviewed, reasons not hired)
- Resume of the beneficiary (Priya)
- Recruitment report (where and when ads ran)
- Employer's prevailing wage documentation
```

sam (Finance): For payroll contingency: we can onboard as contractor for up to 90 days but we'll need: W-9, invoice cadence, and rate approval from legal. Priya, can you accept a 1099 arrangement temporarily?

priya (Newhire): I can do 1099 for a short period but need to confirm taxes. Please send the contract.

megan (People Ops): Ok plan A: proceed with contractor onboarding today to meet start. Plan B: if DOL requests more info or insists on constraints, we'll shift to pending start + benefits hold. Everyone — deadline to upload remaining docs is EOD tomorrow so Alex can submit within 5 business days.

raj (Hiring Manager): Agreed. I'm ok with short-term contractor. @sam please confirm pay rate will match offer so Priya doesn't incur loss.

sam (Finance): Confirmed — we can mirror the base rate as a contractor payment for first 30 days, subject to vendor paperwork.

alex (Immigration Counsel): I'll prepare the audit packet and run it by Megan + Raj before submission. If DOL asks follow-ups, it can add 4–8 weeks typically. Will post status updates here.

megan (People Ops): Thank you all. Priya — I'll DM you the contractor packet and benefits checklist. Ping me immediately once vendor docs are back so we can finalize payroll. :thumbsup:
